title: Probiotic Bifidobacterium Breve PRL2020 in Oral Drops in Preventing Side Effects From Amoxicillin or Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid Antibiotic Use
official: Assessment of the Impact of an Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid-resistant Probiotic on the Reduction of AAD (Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhoea) in Children Treated With Amoxicillin/Clavulanic Acid or Amoxicillin: a Multicentre, Randomised, Placebo-controlled Clinical Trial.
summary: This multicenter, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial will evaluate the efficacy and safety of the probiotic Bifidobacterium breve PRL2020 (Brevicillin® gocce) in preventing gastrointestinal side effects associated with antibiotic therapy using amoxicillin or amoxicillin/clavulanic acid in pediatric patients aged 0-12 years. Participants will be randomized 1:1 to receive either the probiotic supplement or placebo during standard antibiotic treatment for 6-10 days, followed by a post-treatment observation period up to day 15 without probiotic or placebo administration. The primary objective is to assess the reduction in the incidence of antibiotic-associated diarrhea (AAD).
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Patients of either sex
* Age ≤ 12 years
* Requirement to undergo antibiotic treatment with amoxicillin or amoxicillin/clavulanic acid

Exclusion Criteria:

* Use of antibiotic therapy in the 4 weeks prior to enrolment in the study.
* Use of other probiotic products or products containing lactic acid bacteria during the study period.
* Presence of pre-existing diarrhoea in the 4 weeks prior to enrolment.
* Presence of chronic inflammatory bowel disease.
* Presence of immunodeficiency.
* Failure to obtain informed consent from the parent or legal guardian for participation in the study.
* Known allergy to the excipients in the formulation
